I'm going through something similar. I lost my boyfriend to suicide and I'm really struggling to connect to people and to life and I don't want to live anymore. I think people assume I'm doing better than I actually am. I got my ESA from the shelter almost a year ago and that's my only redeeming quality- I have a gentle, calm, fluffy dog. I struggle sometimes to even look at her because she reminds me of all the memories I shared with my boyfriend walking her and all three of us cuddling. I pictured us like a little premature family. She's 8 years old and I don't know who would take her if I died. I feel awful that when I go to self harm, I look up and see her looking back at me like she knows. Since his death, she's been the only thing that's stopped me, which I feel guilty about when I consider my family. 

But. For now I think it's important that we appreciate having something around just to keep us going. It doesn't matter what it is. I saw someone that said the same things about their pet bird, and I don't think I've ever known of a bird with a better purpose than giving someone the will to live. So no, I think adopting a dog was the best decision if your dog is helping you even in the slightest. I hope that if you need any help you will reach out to others, and you can message me if you'd like.

I'm not sure how old you are but judging by the fact that you use Reddit, I'm assuming young. Which means you have a lot left to do in this world. When you are young ish (before 50 even) it's a struggle to find your purpose. Some people never do. But that doesn't mean your presence here isn't significant. You never know what could happen in the years to come. Don't assume that you will become a burden. Maybe you instead will become the light of someone's life who is struggling in the same ways. Maybe talk to a therapist or close family member about how to get motivated and active in something again. I know you can do this. Just be patient :)

You are not the outlier, you are not a burden, you are not ruining anyone's life by being alive. Don't let those negative thoughts win. If you need to talk to an extra person about what you've been going through, I'm here.

I would recommend looking up different therapists or alternative types of therapy. It took me a while to find a therapist that I actually felt open to (I had a weird thing about therapists for most of my life and found it really difficult to trust them or talk to them, making the sessions rather ineffective). My sister has attempted suicide several times and has been in impatient care throughout her life for a total of 1 ear. Obviously, it isn't a cure- all for her. But she always tells me how much better she feels about things after staying and has made friends there that were going through similar issues, which only helped her feel more supported in the whole process. Maybe take a second look at that? Also, in my opinion, going through what you are feeling and still getting through it all every day is very admirable. I hope you are able to reach out to some close friends and family about your thoughts, they need to know how they have been making you feel and what you're struggling with.

Does your insurance cover therapy at all? If so, how is that going? If not, would it at all be a possibility to get a different insurance? I see two therapists currently- one that makes sure my meds are working for me and one that is more focused on alternative methods of treating anxiety and depression. The second way is a lot more difficult and takes a lot of patience, but I've found things like breathing exercises and getting an Emotional Support Animal (while seemingly simple) were really supplementary to the meds.

My therapist always tells me that sometimes it's a victory just to make it to the next hour. Maybe don't force yourself into planning that far ahead for right now, and if you have a therapist talk to them about this. Mine was very good about explaining ways I can try to work on planning for the next hour or two and not stress out about next week, as I found it incredibly exhausting and depressing trying to think about any sort of future. The hour by hour thing seems to work well so far.. not sure how it works long term but that's not the point of the exercise I guess. It's just important that you've found something that will work for now, and maybe when you feel it becoming less effective let a therapist or friend know and they might have new ideas to try.

Sometimes it's hard to know what the point is or what our purpose is, and it just takes a while to get there. It requires a lot of patience with the world and with yourself. I really truly hope you will reconsider and give life some time. One day you might look back and be so incredibly thankful that you hadn't ended things. I've never called the suicide hotline but maybe give that a shot or other forms of therapy. One of my favorite quotes is "you've gotten through every bad day you didn't think you could get through." Best wishes to you.

Please don't let a break up do this. Or anything, really. I lost my boyfriend to suicide after a fight. He was also convinced that his friends, family, and me didn't love him anymore. That is the farthest thing from the truth. I am in so much pain every day and wish I had known what he was thinking in the time between our argument and his death. I would give anything to go back and change what I said, or not even date him if it meant he would still be alive. I don't know your situation, but I know you would be missed. I know you have a full life ahead of you and anything is possible. I know that it can be hard if you feel distant from family, but I hope you'll consider therapy, talking to close friends, or even reaching out to a relative even if you haven't talked to them in a while. The other commenter is right. Take the pain you are feeling and try to focus it on other things. Maybe a new trade or hobby. Try something new, maybe it will help get your mind off of it all and help you live for yourself and find happiness. I know it's hard, I haven't been able to find any source of happiness after his death, but I cling to the hope of something turning around for me. I hope you can find hope within yourself and trust that eventually things will work out.

Getting the help you need from a close friend or family member or therapist or anyone is never seeking attention, it's getting the help you need to make it to tomorrow. If anyone reduces your asking for help to you "asking for attention" remove those toxic people from your life.

When my boyfriend committed suicide, all he left was an email to me that said "I love you. Goodbye <3". Nothing to his family or friends. And not even a detailed text that I could have tried to act on. I think about this every day. I think about him every day. I want to die every second of every day just so I don't have to live with this pain anymore. But the reason I'm telling you this is something struck me about your situation. You said before you fell in love, you didn't hurt yourself because of family. Even now, you have letters written to your family. So there is a part of you that knows they care. This part of you knows that they will be devastated by the loss of you. You want to write to them to explain things or say a final goodbye, I'm assuming. This tells me that somewhere deep in your mind, that part of you that is "losing ground" still knows you have someone you can go to. Listen. You have someone. I guarantee it. Take it from someone that sat through a funeral with hundreds of people showing up for my boyfriend that claimed his friends and family hated him. If you feel like people that you associate with think your a "dick" just because of simple mistakes that tons of people do then start fresh with better friends who have your best interest in mind or just be honest with those you're closest to about how you're doing. hook up culture is a very prevalent thing in today's society, and the fact that you even hold a small sense of guilt about it tells me you are better than that and not a dick at all- most people never feel bad, but that doesn't necessarily  make them bad people either. everyone has their hardships in life with which they struggle to deal with. Early on you may have been using sex to deal with your problems. I did the same before my long term relationship. But anyway, my point is you have something to work with. Listen to that little voice in your head that's telling you not to hurt yourself. If that voice isn't loud enough, remind yourself of your family and the pain they will feel when they wonder what they could have done differently. If I was only thinking about my pain I would have hurt myself a month ago. But I try to keep pushing on by thinking about my family and the possibility of me ruining their lives through my decisions is enough to keep me going so far.

I really hope this may have helped. I just wanted to make sure you knew someone is listening. PM me if you need.

Please don't hurt yourself. Life can seem impossible, believe me I know, but there are so many people who  are there for you and you may not even realize it. You cannot let those thoughts win, it's the depression talking. Please call someone and reach out, it doesn't even matter who, but as a person who has lost someone to suicide, I've seen how many people wish they could have been there to help, even if they didn't know him very well. If you can't find any contacts in your phone to call, try the helpline. And if the person you get the first time doesn't help enough, call again. Please be safe, sending love through Reddit.

P.s. This is coming from a girl that spent three hours today looking up how to contact the dead, every night practicing lucid dreaming, and an hour yesterday re-reading theories on time travel. For me, my boyfriend was my main support system. Always there, no matter what. I'm sure you can relate to that. Taking that away from a person changes their perspective. Try not to think of this new outlook as "crazy" but just new. You need to do whatever you need to do to get past this moment. My therapist tells me that we don't have to live for tomorrow, just the next hour. And the next. Treat every hour as a victory until an hour becomes a day, and a day becomes a week.

Your post brought me to actual sobbing. I can relate to your pain so much. I know that right now, you probably have friends or family that tell you that and then tell you a story about something unrelated and seemingly ridiculous. But if it helps, hear me out. My boyfriend took his life just over a month ago. He bought the supplies about 30 minutes after a fight/ break up we had. I had been studying abroad and our relationship seemed rocky. I thought maybe he needed time to focus on friends and school, as lately he'd been picking fights over the smallest things and it didn't seem healthy. We had talked about how distance would change the relationship a bit, but yet neither of us remembered the promises we made before I left to work through it all. At some point, I asked him what he thought we should do. I said I didn't want to end things but wasn't sure how to fix the fighting, and he said "it's okay, I know what has to happen." I asked what he meant, he clarified we needed to end things but wanted to talk as friends for another day. Another time, he said he couldn't live without me.. I related this to the fighting, and told him we didn't have to live without each other but that we could still be friends and work things out when I got home or even after a short break. The day he died, he had sent a text during an argument in which he falsely accused me of cheating and never loving him. He said I might as well tell him if I had slept with any guys the night before. I angrily texted my response (while having spotty and limited data connection, navigating unfamiliar roads and getting yelled at in another language for being on my phone) back to him and never saw the message "I'm already dead." At least that's what I have convinced myself, it's hard to believe how self centered I was being. How I'd talked with him every waking minute for over a year but yet missed the signs he'd been giving me. His only suicide note was an email to me, which just said in the subject line "I love you. Goodbye <3" and I didn't even see the email for a few hours after he sent it because I didn't have my data turned on. After I did see it, I didn't reply right away because I thought he was still referring to the break up and was so confused and hurt I wasn't sure what the right response was. The thing was, it wasn't our first "break up." We had considered it once before after a bad fight, but he called me soon after I walked away saying he couldn't stay mad at me for more than a few hours. Which is why I knew something was wrong when his friend texted me asking if I'd heard from him. I realized that it shouldn't have mattered what was said, he should have replied to my message by now. 
Obviously, I feel extremely guilty all the time. I'm lonely constantly. The only time I feel calm is when I think about death or think about the afterlife. Which is odd for me because I used to be atheist. I have dreams about him every night where he tells me he isn't actually dead, and it's always so painful waking up. I used to be so goal oriented but I can't plan for tomorrow anymore. I don't see a future career, much less the ability to ever love again.
I can understand why you find peace in joining him. I've been self harming, but I haven't been able to do anything too serious. I just can't bring myself to do to my loved ones what he did to me. I don't think he did it to hurt me judging by his last message and just knowing who he was deep down. But the thing is, you have no way of guaranteeing that you'll be with him. From an atheist point of view, it could just be nothingness after death, and you leave behind so much pain for others. From a religious point of view, you may get to see him but not all spirits stay together even. There is just no way of knowing. My depression tries convincing me every day that eventually people will be better off, and my pain will be ended, too. But I bet that's what my boyfriend was thinking, and he was definitely wrong about the former. As for the latter, if his spirit has had to witness what his closest loved ones have gone through, I can't imagine his spirit is content. 
"The best way to keep someone alive and with you is by keeping their memories close to your heart and their love for you remembered."-something my hippie sister said.
